literal: Folly that which is called one thing, what if asked, harm taking, benefit to go letting go.
translation: If one asks what that single thing called folly is, it is taking hold of what is harmful and letting go of what is beneficial.
modern: பேதைமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு தன்மை யாது என்று கேட்டால், அது தனக்குத் துன்பம் தருவனவற்றை ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு, நன்மை தருவனவற்றைத் நழுவவிடுவது ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core nature of folly. The poet asks a rhetorical question about what constitutes folly, and answers it directly. Folly is the lack of discernment that leads a person to actively embrace things that bring harm (ētam) while letting go of things that bring true benefit (ūtiyam). A foolish person acts against their own self-interest, choosing ruin over prosperity.
